body_markdown:
**AMARILLO, Texas** (Nov. 13, 2026) — As colder weather approaches Texas and New Mexico, Xcel Energy is reminding customers of tips and programs to help them save on their energy bills. Xcel Energy also offers payment plans and encourages customers to reach out if they are having trouble paying their bills.


**Take steps to save**


-


Lower the thermostat by a few degrees.


-


Install a smart thermostat to automatically lower the temperature when away from home or during overnight hours.


-


Replace or clean your furnace filter every three months or when it looks dirty, helping it work more efficiently.


-


Open drapes and blinds during the day to let sunlight in and retain heat. Keep them closed when it’s dark.


-


Run ceiling fans clockwise to push warm air down.


-


Open interior doors to circulate warm air and maintain constant heating levels.


-


Bundle up before turning the heat up.


Additional[energy savings tips](https://tx.my.xcelenergy.com/s/residential/tips) and information about programs, incentives and rebates to help make homes and businesses more energy efficient are available at xcelenergy.com.


Xcel Energy also reminds customers that they can take control of their electric bills with[payment programs](https://tx.my.xcelenergy.com/s/billing-payment/manage-bill) , including:


-


Payment Arrangement, which allows customers to split bills into smaller amounts.


-


Average Monthly Payment, which offers predictable monthly bills.


-


Custom Due Date.


“We know that families are facing tighter budgets, and our team is here to help,” said Randy Cantu, senior director of contact center operations in Amarillo. “We want customers who are struggling to reach out to us to discuss their options. It’s about keeping them warm and safe this winter, while making it easier on their wallets.”


Customers are encouraged to reach out before they fall behind as Xcel Energy customer service agents are available to provide payment plans and connect customers with energy assistance programs in their communities. More information and resources can be found at **xcelenergy.com** or by calling 1-800-395-4999.
